"The McPherson Tape" is an early (some argue the first) "found footage" film about a rural family's encounter with extraterrestrials. Its shot-on-VHS, rough around the edges quality was so effective at selling the aliens that the tape was sold in many markets as evidence of an encounter.

"Motel Hell" is what my mother would affectionately call "a drive-in movie." This film stuck in her memory, and I remember her excitement at finding it at the video store. A delightfully strange and campy film about a farmer (Rory Calhoun at his best) famous for his mysterious smoked meats.

Keeping up the camp cannibalism is "Eating Raoul", Paul Bartel's dark comedy about the lengths a repressed couple will go to realize their dream of opening a restaurant. Always love seeing who picks this one in their Criterion closet videos (Peter Sarsgaard, Sean Baker, and Wallace Shawn grabbed it)
